title: M/Y Biscayne Lady
subtitle: Yacht money-laundering bust (a Miami Vice homage)
briefing: TOC: Element, Miami Beach Marina, slip 14. The Biscayne Lady is a 90-foot motor yacht registered to a shell company in the Caymans. She belongs to Fuente. Every dollar his network makes comes aboard this boat to be counted, bricked and run to the Bahamas, where it comes back clean through a private bank.

Fuente never does business on land. He runs everything on the water so that at the first sign of trouble the money goes over the side. Expect his middleman Reydolfo and an accountant counting cash in the main salon, a banker from Nassau in the guest cabin, and Fuente in the master stateroom below. Reydolfo's people WILL dump the cash if they hear you coming.

She's fueled, provisioned, and getting ready to leave. The captain is on the bridge running his checklist, and once he hears trouble he'll cut the lines and go. If the Biscayne Lady leaves the dock, this operation is over. Take the bridge, or the captain, early.

Security: an armed man on the aft deck watching the pier, another on the swim platform by the tender, and one below in the engine room. The crew (deckhand, chef, mechanic) and Fuente's guest are civilians. If things go bad, Fuente and the banker will try for the tender off the stern. Harbor patrol has a boat for you at the stern if you want it.

Objectives: arrest or neutralize every suspect, secure every civilian, and recover the cash duffels, the bricked cash and the shell company ledger. Report everyone to TOC. Rules of engagement: deadly force only against a suspect who is visibly armed and not surrendering. Bring order to chaos.

departure.warning: the Biscayne Lady's engines are running and the lines are coming off
departure.departed: The last line drops and the Biscayne Lady swings away from the dock, throttles open, headed for open water. TOC: "Harbor patrol has her. Element, stand down. We lost them."

rooms.name: Pier
rooms.desc: Slip 14 at the Miami Beach Marina. Pastel sunset, palm trees and pelicans, and a gangway up to the aft deck of a long white motor yacht.

rooms.name: Patrol Boat
rooms.desc: A harbor patrol boat idling quietly off the yacht's stern. The swim platform and its stern gate are a short step across.

rooms.name: Aft Deck
rooms.desc: Teak deck, a wet bar and white cushions. Sliding glass doors lead into the salon, a ladder climbs to the bridge, and the transom gate drops to the swim platform.

rooms.name: Swim Platform
rooms.desc: A low platform at the stern, just above the water. A tender is tied off here with its outboard tipped down, ready to go.

rooms.name: Main Salon
rooms.desc: White leather, mirrors and a glass coffee table buried in rubber-banded cash. Two cash counters whir side by side, and duffel bags sit open on the carpet.

rooms.name: Galley
rooms.desc: A gleaming galley with something on the stove. Crew stairs lead down to the lower deck.

rooms.name: Bridge
rooms.desc: The helm, with radar, chart plotter and twin throttles. The windshield looks out over the bow at the harbor mouth.

rooms.name: Lower Hall
rooms.desc: A narrow mahogany passage. Doors lead to the master and guest staterooms, and a hatch leads to the engine room.

rooms.name: Master Stateroom
rooms.desc: A king berth, mirrored ceiling and a desk with a ledger open beside a phone. Portholes look out at the waterline.

rooms.name: Guest Cabin
rooms.desc: A small cabin with two berths, a packed briefcase and a garment bag. Someone's ready to travel.

rooms.name: Engine Room
rooms.desc: Twin diesels ticking hot. A panel behind the generator is open, and vacuum-sealed cash bricks are being stacked inside.
